1.20.betting_forecast: 6/4 Edward Thatch, 9/2 Bit Of A Buzz, 13/2 Matriarchal, 10/1 Eighteenth Smiles, Nation Blaze, Queenofthewild, 11/1
1.20.spotlight_verdict: EDWARD THATCH showed plenty of early speed before fading late at the Curragh and he can make amends on this better ground with this track likely to suit. Matriarchal and Bit Of A Buzz both showed potential last time and they hold place claims at least. Nation Blaze, Ballymackney and Queenofthewild appeal most of the newcomers. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: Earthlight filly; E20,000 yearling; dam unraced half-sister to Italian Listed winners Fast Spirit (7f/7.5f 2yo) and Bright Filly (6f 2yo), out of sister to winners Lethal Promise (5.5f/6f Listed) and Promising (Group-placed 6f); worth monitoring in the market.
Showed ability when weakening late into a 5.75l third behind Force Noir at Naas six days ago; likely to improve for that first run and this easier 5f should suit; place shout.

Kodi Bear colt; 34,000gns yearling; closely related to 1m AW 2yo winner Booziebrunch (RPR 73); dam Listed-placed 5f 2yo/6.5f winner (99), half-sister to winners Snap Shots (5f/6f inc 2yo) and Zebedaios (6f-1m); likely best watched on debut.

Blackbeard colt sent off at even money on debut at the Curragh (5f, sft-hvy) but could only manage a 3.5l third of 8 after showing lots of early speed; pedigree suggests that better ground will suit, as will this easier 5f; leading chance.

State Of Rest colt; dam 12.6f winner (RPR 83), closely related to 11.6f Listed winner Perfect Clarity, half-sister to Italian 1m2f Listed winner Law Power; pedigree suggests this trip may be too sharp.

Kodi Bear colt; E30,000 yearling; brother to 6f/7f winner Noor Bano (inc UAE; RPR 97), half-brother to Qatari winners Tashkent (6f) and Ponga (7f 2yo); dam Listed-placed 7f-8.4f winner (inc 2yo; 102), half-sister to dam of 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Sioux Nation; nicely bred but yard not known for 2yo winners; watch.

Sioux Nation filly sent off at 18-1 on debut in six runner maiden at Dundalk and was beaten just 2l into fourth despite racing keenly and running green; can improve for that and place claims if she acts on turf.

Sioux Nation colt; E52,000 yearling; dam unplaced 5f (RPR 44), half-sister to winners Parkes And Ride (Qatari 7f/1m), Cape Castle (1m4f-1m6f; dam of 1m2f Group 1 winner Thundering Nights) and Influent (1m/9.4f); respected source; check the market.

Bungle Inthejungle filly; E38,000 yearling; dam 5f winner (RPR 79), half-sister to winners One More Word (Listed-placed 7f-1m inc 2yo), Archers Road (5f inc 2yo) and Somalian (1m inc 2yo); worth a market check on debut.
Not a bad effort on debut at the Curragh when a 12.5l fourth, green before making modest late gains; was 9l behind Edward Thatch, however, so much more needed to turn the tables on that rival.
Soldier's Call colt beaten 20l on debut at the Curragh when well behind Edward Thatch; huge improvement needed to turn that form around.

Soldier's Call filly; E7,000 yearling; sister to French 6.5f AW 2yo winner Finders Keepers; dam 5.7f turf/7f AW winner (RPR 84), half-sister to useful 6f-1m2f winner Mr Scaramanga; likely to improve for this initial experience.

1.55.betting_forecast: 15/8 The Piper's Call, 11/4 Cool Azul, 4/1 Sparky Sparky, 10/1 Ragaire, Xerling, 12/1 Samurai Mike, 14/1 Dreaminthejungle,
1.55.spotlight_verdict: With the benefit of an initial outing at the Curragh, COOL AZUL has good prospects of coping with obvious danger The Piper's Call who showed potential in his two starts at two. Sparky Sparky is another with a clear chance. Ragaire may not have been suited by testing ground first time out. [Alan Sweetman]

horses.spotlight_comment: May improve from debut at this venue last month; has a bit to find with third-placed Sparky Sparky.
Finished in mid-field over 1m at Gowran on debut, not guaranteed to improve over his trip.
No threat on AW on debut; down the field in Curragh race in which Cool Azul was second.

Half-brother to winners, notably Last Crusader, a 5f Listed scorer for Karl Burke; dam French Group-placed 6f 2yo winner; in front of useful yardstick Starman Tom (Listed-placed since) when second on debut in a 24-runner maiden at the Curragh; winner Thenandnow runs in the Listed race later on; could be hard to beat from a low draw.

Shaped promisingly when seventh of 16 over 6f at the Curragh on only start last year; fine effort against younger rivals when fifth of 24 at the same venue on reappearance; held by runner-up Cool Azul.
Needs to step up on the form of two juvenile outings at the Curragh to feature here.
Did not show enough first time out at Gowran to suggest she can pose a serious threat.
47,000gns yearling; eighth foal; brother to 5f Listed winner winner Dickiedooda, closely related to 1m4f AW winner Sioux Princess (69); dam French AW 2yo winner, half-sister to two Listed winners.
Slowly away/never in contention when 40-1 on debut in a 1m maiden at Gowran 11 days ago.
28,000gns yearling; Due Diligence gelding is the second foal out of 7f AW 2yo winner.
No sign of worthwhile form in three outings last season, two of them at this venue.

85,000gns foal, 400,000gns yearling; third foal; increase in purchase price from foal to yearling is noteworthy; however, made no show on debut in the Curragh race in which Cool Azul was second; 15-2 chance then, so that was presumably too bad to be true.
70,000gns yearling; third foal; gelded son of Starspangledbanner; dam Listed winner in Italy; could go well first time out.
Confirmed promise of Naas fourth last year with third placing over 5f here on reappearance; should not be far away, but collateral form involving Starman Tom suggests he might not cope with Cool Azul

Sent off at 80-1 on debut for a Curragh maiden but belied those odds with an excellent second of 13 behind subsequent Group 3 runner-up Flushing Meadows; form advertised, notably by the top-class Puerto Rico; again showed winning potential when third behind a Ballydoyle-trained colt at Naas; gelded now.
Ninth foal; half-brother to Listed scorer Ocean Vision and two other winners; dam Listed-placed 7f winner, half-sister to US 7f Grade 2 winner/good broodmare Letgomyecho.
Fair 6f Naas maiden run on her second outing; out of her depth in a 5f Listed race at Dundalk last October; should be more at home in this company.
Third foal; half-sister by Kessaar to an Italian 5f winner; dam 7f AW winner; stable's current form is a positive

2.30.betting_forecast: 5/1 Aviatrice, 6/1 Collecting Coin, Key Witness, 7/1 Gleneagle Bay, 8/1 Dmaniac, Final Voyage, Nancy J, 10/1 Brewing, Gerrit's
2.30.spotlight_verdict: A return to 7f could do the trick for COLLECTING COIN who appeared to be outstayed over 1m at Limerick recently. Likely dangers are Key Witness, who has prospered at the Curragh since joining Pat Flynn, and Aviatrice, a Listed winner at Dundalk on her final start last season. Glenesgle Bay appeals on last season's form but needs to rebound after a low-key reappearance. [Alan Sweetman]

horses.spotlight_comment: Promoted to 95 on AW after Listed win at Dundalk last November, her third win from six starts at that track; runs off 7lb lower here; a likely player if ready, since she showed her effectiveness on turf with a couple of placed runs last August.
horses.breeding: b f Phoenix Of Spain - Virtudes

horses.spotlight_comment: All six wins have been gained on AW; in good form at Dundalk this winter before a below-par Newcastle run on latest; others have much stronger claims on turf form.

Consistent form last season included a Galway maiden win (7f, yielding); sound effort on handicap debut and seasonal return at Naas (7f, soft); did not quite see out the 1m trip when a close-up fourth at Limerick eight days ago; return to 7f could make all the difference.
horses.breeding: b g Lope De Vega - Mighty Spirit

horses.spotlight_comment: Won over 6f at the Curragh on final start of 2025 and reappeared with another 6f win at the same venue; beaten favourite over 5f last time; winning form points to a preference for testing conditions.
Four wins in France; testing ground conditions not ideal on his Irish debut at the Curragh; tough task under a big weight here.
Only two wins from 22 Flat starts, placed nine times; below best on seasonal debut in Curragh event won by today's rival Key Witness.
All three wins have come at this venue, twice over 6f, the other coming at 1m; liking for the track is enough to make him worth considering on stable/seasonal debut.

Sole win came on debut at Dundalk in March 2024; 0-12 since but ran well in top handicaps last season, including fifth in Irish Lincoln, third in Victoria Cup at Ascot and second in Ahonoora at Galway; flopped when fancied (5-1) on return in race won by Key Witness; not ruled out.

7f maiden winner on the AW for Archie Watson; has prospered at the Curragh since joining Pat Flynn, ending last season with a 7f win and starting the new campaign with a 1m success; goes well for this rider whose claim is now reduced to 5lb.
Maiden winner at two; struggled in handicaps in the first half of last season for Jessica Harrington and never counted on yard debut last October; not much better on reappearance.
horses.breeding: br f Bated Breath - Grace Note

3.05.betting_forecast: 4/6 Havana Anna, 5/1 Quiet Mutiny, 11/2 Ipanema Queen, 8/1 Royal Bay Cen, 12/1 Bear On The Run, Oh Cecelia, Rosie Frith,
3.05.spotlight_verdict: Runner-up in the Cheveley Park, HAVANA ANNA will be hard to beat if near peak form for her first run since a Breeders' Cup reverse. Her most interesting opponent is Grey Mutiny who beat the top-class Precise with a fair degree of comfort on her only start at two. Ipanema Queen has the advantage of a run under her belt. Royal Bay Cen reached a good standard of form in France. [Alan Sweetman]

horses.spotlight_comment: Started with a respectable fifth of 14 at the Curragh last May; made all to win over the same trip at Dundalk on August on her only other start at two; half-sister to 5f Group 3 winner Dun Na Sead, worth a shot at this.
Beaten 6l by Havana Anna over 5f at Naas on her debut; won a 6f maiden at the same venue on good ground on her third start; in rear in a 6f Listed race at Fairyhouse in September.

Maiden and Listed winner over 5f; beaten only a nose in a Group 3 over the minimum trip at Longchamp, though produced her best effort when chasing home True Love in the 6f Group 1 Cheveley Park; failed to cope with the challenge of the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint; the clear pick on overall form.
horses.breeding: b f Havana Grey - Miss Villefranche

horses.spotlight_comment: Won a 6f Curragh maiden on debut but seemed better suited to 5f as the season progressed; won two Listed races at the Curragh and Dundalk over the minimum trip after finishing 3 3/4l second to Havana Anna at Naas; lost out narrowly to a longer-priced stablemate at Dundalk on seasonal debut; should reach the money.
horses.breeding: b f Sands Of Mali - No More Thrills

horses.spotlight_comment: Has run 11 times, with two of her three wins gained over C&D; failed to progress from a maiden win last May; sold for 9,000GBP in January and got back to form in winning a 5f Naas handicap on stable debut; fifth in a 6f handicap at the Curragh early here last month; reappeared over C&D the following day to win a 5f conditions race; more on her plate.

22,000gns yearling; first foal; dam 6f winner from the family of outstanding sprinter Lochsong; justified good support on debut in a 6f maiden at Fairyhouse last July; the form could hardly have worked out better, runner-up Precise won her next four races, completing a Group 1 double in the Moyglare and Fillies' Mile.

C&D maiden winner last July on the fourth of eight stats at two; beaten a nose in an auction series race over 6f at this venue before going down by a neck in a 5f Dundalk event; signed off with a nursery win at Dundalk; struggled on her only run in a stakes race.
horses.breeding: b f Cotai Glory - Mary Frith

horses.spotlight_comment: Dual 6f winner in France at two; posted her two best efforts in defeat in a 7f Group 3 at Longchamp and a 6f Group 3 at Chantilly; has never run over 5f, but her dam Royal Razalma won the Cornwallis.
horses.breeding: ch f New Bay - Royal Razalma

horses.spotlight_comment: Officially rated 75 after four runs at two, the best of which was a 1 3/4l second of eight on debut at Leopardstown (7f, good-to-firm); now promoted to 85 after winning a 24-runner maiden at the Curragh; that was not a strong race, and she faces a tough task now.

Narrowly beaten twice in Naas fillies' maidens before landing the odds in a seven-runner C&D maiden last September; outpaced in the closing stages in a 5f Listed race at Dundalk in October; not suited by the race conditions, but stable in good form.

3.43.betting_forecast: 6/1 Genoah, Perry Mason, 7/1 Kilmeaden, Navy Waters, 10/1 Alba Chiara, Lifting Sails, Truth Be Told, 12/1 Comfort Zone,
3.43.spotlight_verdict: In an open race NAVY WATERS gets the vote in the hope that she can improve from her seasonal debut at Navan. Race fitness should be an asset in a rematch of last autumn's Down Royal clash with runner-up Alba Chiara. One of the less exposed runners is Lifting Sails who has a clear chance if forgiven a failure at Lingfield. Perry Mason could benefit if the ground deteriorates. That might not suit Genoah who seems to be an AW specialist. [Alan Sweetman]

horses.spotlight_comment: All her best form has been at Down Royal, a win and two seconds, one of them behind today's rival Navy Waters; sent on a long journey from Northern Ireland for this; could go well.
Three-time hurdle winner went close in 2m4f Ascot Stakes last June; finished well when close third in 2m Naas handicap in October; this trip is on the short side.

A Leopardstown specialist, winning three times there last season over 1m5f, including a premier handicap in September; never a factor in the Irish Cesarewitch; needs to step up from his seasonal debut at the Curragh.
Last year's Galway Hurdle runner-up, a long time since the last of his five Flat wins (enjoyed highlight in the Group 1 Tattersalls Gold Cup in 2021); slipping in the ratings and fit from hurdling.
Maiden hurdle and three-time Flat winner; found 1m2f inadequate on seasonal debut; extra couple of furlongs here should help.
Struggled with the surface at Lingfield last November; showed plenty of ability on turf with a wide-margin maiden win at Bellewstown, and is relatively unexposed; one for the shortlist.
horses.breeding: ch f Raven's Pass - Gold Zain

horses.spotlight_comment: Won a 1m6f conditions race and two races over hurdles in 2025; lacks a recent outing and possibly more effective as a hurdler at this stage of his career.

His good Curragh form late last season and early this term has been on very soft ground; also testing when he won at Galway last October; any rain would improve his prospects, further drying would be a negative.
On the upgrade on first two 2026 turf runs; 5lb out of the handicap; more needed.
horses.breeding: b g Rock Of Gibraltar - Shes An Art

horses.spotlight_comment: Seven-time winner, on a long losing sequence now; unplaced in two outings this term; others have stronger credentials.
horses.breeding: b g Sea The Stars - Sioduil

horses.spotlight_comment: Five-time winner has yet to score in a handicap; won a 1m6f conditions race at Galway for the second year running last August; poor run over 1m6f on seasonal debut; stable appears to have two stronger contenders.
Appreciated to step up in trip when winning at Thurles on his final start last season; further improvement possible for his new trainer.
horses.breeding: b g Too Darn Hot - Princess Highway

4.15.betting_forecast: 100/30 Arctic Assassin, 4/1 Johnny Soda, 11/2 Kalir, 13/2 Harmani, 7/1 L L Koulsty, 10/1 Matilda Joslyngage, 11/1 Venetian
4.15.spotlight_verdict: The recent Curragh winner Arctic Assassin has gone up 9lb and may not uphold form with Johnny Soda, who is weighted to turn the tables. Both may have to give best to the previous course winner L L KOULSTY who shaped as though the step back up to a mile would suit at the Curragh last time and he's 1lb lower now. Kalir, Matilda Joslyngage and Harmani are potential improvers on their handicap debuts. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: Left ordinary maiden form behind to win a 1m Curragh handicap (soft) by 0.75l on seasonal return two weeks ago, beating a couple of these rivals in the process; 9lb rise partly negated by useful rider's 4lb claim; should go well again.

Modest form in maidens and similar story on handicap debut at Naas last September (1m, soft) when an 11l sixth of 16; met trouble in running when clipping heels and unseating on return at Limerick eight days ago; yard in form and too early to write off.
horses.breeding: b f Kodi Bear - Zero Turn

horses.spotlight_comment: Kept busy at two, winning one of his 10 starts; that win came at Dundalk (7f) in December off 72; went close in a 1m turf claimer on seasonal return at Gowran (soft); dropped 4lb for poor run at Naas (6f, good) six days ago; Johnny Soda looks yard's main hope.
Handicap debutante's best maiden run her latest at Leopardstown (1m, gd-yld) but was still beaten 11l; likely best watched here unless the market suggests otherwise.
horses.breeding: gr f Sottsass - Hug And A Kiss

horses.spotlight_comment: Placed in two of three maidens; beaten 5.5l on debut when runner up at Navan (6f, soft) behind Charles Darwin; 3-1 favourite but faded when beaten 7.75l on seasonal return in a Gowran maiden (7f, soft); sharper for that and should get 1m on breeding; could go well on handicap debut.
horses.breeding: gr g Phoenix Of Spain - Martine's Spirit

horses.spotlight_comment: Promise in maidens last season, including when fourth of 16 over C&D (yielding); two maiden runs this term below that level and now switches to a handicap for the first time; yard in form and potentially well treated on the form of that C&D run last year; check the market.

(4) 7-1 79 72 77 Course winner last season at 6f (yld-sft); respectable run in 1m Newcastle novice (AW) in February and pleasing return to turf on handicap debut at the Curragh two weeks ago (7f, soft); step back up to 1m a plus; cheekpieces retained; big player off 1lb lower.

Modest form first two maidens at 7f but big step forward upped to 1m at Thurles (gd-yld) last October when a 1.75l runner up behind Killashee Warrior (now rated 94); could go well on handicap debut if ready after a 206-day absence.

Best effort last season a 1.5l second on handicap debut at Down Royal (7f, good); 4l behind Arctic Assassin on seasonal return at the Curragh; weighted to close the gap to that rival and should strip fitter but might prefer quicker ground.
horses.breeding: b g Starman - Mistress Of Venice

4.50.betting_forecast: 11/4 Yousaynothingatall, 7/2 Contrite, 11/2 Dreamkeeper, 13/2 Lake Bonney, 11/1 Themis, 12/1 Aravalli, Miss Romagna, 16/1
4.50.spotlight_verdict: After a solid run in a handicap here last time Yousaynothingatall has to be considered returned to maiden company but she might be worth taking on with MISS ROMAGNA. She was badly hampered when making headway up the inside at Leopardstown and can turn the tables on Lake Bonney, who finished just 2.75l ahead of her in fourth that day. Dreamkeeper and Contrite complete the shortlist. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: Beaten cumulative distance of 44l in maidens at Leopardstown (1m, yielding) last year and the Curragh (1m2f, heavy) on seasonal return; much more needed.

Churchill filly; 20,000gns yearling; closely related to Italian 6f winner Soaring Eagle; dam French 7f winner (RPR 74), sister to US 6f/6.5f winner Consortium, out of US 8.5f/1m1f Grade 3 winner; this trip might stretch stamina on breeding.
Well-related Teofilo filly outran her odds of 16-1 when a 5.25l fourth of 14 on debut at Dundalk in November (1m); bred to stay this far and worth a market check on seasonal reappearance.

Sent off at 80-1 on debut at Navan (1m2f, gd-yld) but ran a promising race to finish sixth of 18, keeping on well; likely to improve plenty for that initial experience and yard remains in fine form; chance.
Modest form so far in maidens at the Curragh (7f, sft-hvy) last October and at Leopardstown (1m, yld-sft) last month; moves up in trip; others have stronger credentials.

Encouraging effort on debut at Leopardstown (1m, yld-sft) last month, keeping on from midfield for a 7.75l fourth of 14 (2.75l ahead of Miss Romagna who was hampered); should improve for that and she's related to plenty of winners; dam won at 1m2f; in the mix.

Sea The Moon filly; E55,000 yearling; half-sister to yard's Group-placed 1m winner Queen Of Thunder (RPR 109); dam 1m2f AW winner (91), half-sister to smart 6.5f/7f winner Parfait; nicely bred and market can guide.

Traffic problems when beaten 10.5l at Leopardstown on debut (2.25l behind Lake Bonney); not given a hard race after meeting interference 2f out; would be no surprise if she reversed form with Lake Bonney granted a clearer run here.
Japan filly; E20,000 yearling; half-sister to Czech/Slovak 1m2f/1m4f winner Paras; dam twice-raced German 1m winner, half-sister to German 1m Listed winner Peace Of Rose; market best guide.

Elzaam filly; dam unraced half-sister to winners The Navigator (1m-1m6f Flat and prolific 2m-2m5f hurdle), Mustique (6f 2yo) and Renaissance (5f-1m inc 2yo); tongue tied and likely best watched on debut.
12-1 for debut at the Curragh (7f, good) last August and failed to beat a rival home; bred to do better than that at some stage but McMonagle jumps ship.

Rated 80 after four starts; okay form in maidens at 1m-10.5f; narrowly denied on handicap debut upped to 1m4f here last month; drop back to this trip a plus on the evidence of that effort; big player.
horses.breeding: b f Australia - Dont Ask Me At All

horses.spotlight_comment: Moderate efforts in maidens at Dundalk and Limerick last month; will find her level in handicaps.

5.27.betting_forecast: 5/4 Atomic City, 6/1 Gaelic Drills, 7/1 Amrum, 15/2 Sunrush, 8/1 Abbotsford, 10/1 Frank Pickle, Roi Du Nord, 12/1 Maxminelli,
5.27.spotlight_verdict: Joseph O'Brien's ATOMIC CITY (nap) has shown promise in both starts and should be able to shed the maiden tag with this better ground likely to suit. Gaelic Drills and Frank Pickle can fight it out for minor money and the nicely bred debutant Hard Promises needs monitoring in the market. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: Frankel colt was sent off at just 9-2 on debut at Dundalk in December (1m) but missed the break and never really threatened; surely capable of better and bred to stay this longer trip but a bit to prove.
Well-bred but failed to get involved when beaten 9.5l on debut in a 1m Dundalk maiden last month; needs to improve plenty upped in trip but it's still very early days so that's not impossible.

Identical RPRs of 75 for sole start last season (1m, heavy) and seasonal return when beaten 0.75l into third of 8 over 1m1f on bottomless ground, both at the Curragh; McMonagle takes over now and should improve for better ground and the step up in trip; leading chance.
Rating of 67 flatters him on what he has shown in four Flat starts; heavy defeat over hurdles latest; now with a fourth different trainer and hard to fancy.

0-7 on the Flat and rated 74; went closest when beaten a head at the Curragh off this mark last August (1m4f, good); beaten 7.5l when fourth in 1m handicap at the Curragh on latest; place chance but wouldn't want to see much rain.
Offered something to build on with a keeping on 6.75l fifth of 11 on debut at Leopardstown (1m2f, yld-sft) 18 days ago; open to plenty of improvement and should go well.

Pinatubo colt; E32,000 yearling; half-brother to winners Sidiriya (1m4f; RPR 86) and Sidiza (1m2f; 83); dam 9.4f winner (91), out of 11.6f Listed winner, from family of Derby and Arc winner Sinndar; plenty to like on paper and stable can ready one; check market.
Rated 69 after three maiden runs at 7f-1m2f; beaten 11.5l when seventh of 13 at Navan on latest (1m2f, heavy); new tongue tie needs to eke out much more.
Huge odds and ran accordingly in two maidens at Gowran and over C&D last month; seems safe to rule out.
Long odds and soundly beaten in maidens at the Curragh last October and here last month; will qualify for handicaps after this.

French recruit; beaten 0.75l over 1m4f on the AW on sole start for Francis Graffard in March 2025; bought for E6,000 at Arqana in July; best watched on seasonal return and stable debut after absence unless the market speaks.
Heavy defeats at Leopardstown and over this C&D on latest; others preferred.
Yard in form but this colt produced two moderate efforts in maidens last season at Tipperary (7f, yielding) and the Curragh (7f, yld-sft); probably best watched upped in trip on seasonal return.
